results.title: Stocks to Watch as the Fed Raises Interest Rates
results.body: Analysts from Mirae Asset Sekuritas Indonesia and RHB Sekuritas Indonesia recommend focusing on BBCA, BBRI, ELSA, MYOR, MDKA, MIKA, SMSM, LSIP and EXCL, citing consensus 12‑month target prices of Rp8,154, Rp3,851, Rp1,103, Rp2,483, Rp3,961, Rp2,715, Rp2,250, Rp1,933 and Rp3,267 respectively as of 21 September 2026, and noting that a majority of analysts rate BBCA and BBRI as buys. These recommendations follow the Federal Reserve’s 25‑basis‑point rate hike to a 3.75‑4 % target range last week, which is expected to tighten global monetary policy and increase funding costs for Indonesian equities.

results.title: XLSMART Telecom Sejahtera Tbk raises 2026 capitalized capex guidance to Rp20 trillion from Rp15 trillion to fund 5G expansion and spectrum optimization
results.body: PT XLSMART Telecom Sejahtera Tbk increased its 2026 capitalized capital expenditure guidance to Rp20 trillion from Rp15 trillion, directing the additional investment toward network infrastructure strengthening, 5G service expansion, and optimization of 700 MHz and 2.6 GHz spectrum utilization. As of the first half of 2026, the company's 5G services covered more than 50 cities with approximately 15,000 base stations reaching 23% of the national population, and its network earned four Ookla awards including Best Mobile Network and Best 5G Network. The company is also collaborating with Google to offer Gemini AI Plus and Cloud Storage to customers, while emphasizing that digital infrastructure development requires ecosystem collaboration among government, operators, technology firms, and device manufacturers. In the second half of 2026, XLSMART will prioritize customer experience enhancement, spectrum optimization, 5G network and ecosystem expansion, and digital service strengthening.

results.title: IHSG September 2026 Outlook Highlights Potential Volatility Amid Global Risks
results.body: The article discusses the September 2026 outlook for Indonesia’s composite index (IHSG), warning that global monetary‑policy events could increase volatility. Kiwoom Sekuritas notes the index rose 5.06% in August but historically posts a –0.94% average return in September, projecting a trading range of 6,400‑6,705 and a 40‑45% chance of a positive close versus a 33% historical probability. Analysts also cite a 34% FedWatch probability of a rate hike, US Treasury yields around 4.6‑4.7% (10‑year) and 4.2‑4.3% (2‑year), and suggest that commodity price strength may support commodity‑linked emitters such as INCO, ANTM and JSMR. The report lists several stocks that could benefit or be pressured, including BBCA, BBNI, BBRI, BMRI, BBTN, CPIN, CTRA, INDF, ITMG, JSMR, TPIA, EXCL, INCO, ANTM, PANI, MTEL, JPFA and KLBF with specific target prices.

results.title: Early trade shows IHSG slipping to 6,506 amid Fed rate‑hike expectations and MSCI rebalancing
results.body: The Jakarta Composite Index (IHSG) opened weaker, down 11.86 points (0.18%) to 6,506 at 09:15 WIB on 31 August 2026. Trading volume reached 5.28 billion shares with a value of Rp2.43 trillion, while 328 stocks rose, 195 fell and 197 were unchanged, and foreign investors recorded a net sell of Rp1.31 trillion the previous week. Analysts from BRI Danareksa, Phintraco, CGS International and Panin linked the move to a rising Fed rate‑hike probability of 59% (per CME FedWatch), the effective MSCI rebalancing on 31 August and heightened geopolitical tension. The day’s recommended equities were BBNI, BFIN, VKTR, BBCA, TLKM, DSSA, BBRI, EXCL, INDY, MDKA, EMAS, PWON, MAPA, MAPI, BBYB and SMRA.

results.title: Summary of stock recommendations for 31 August 2026
results.body: The article provides a broker‑compiled list of recommended Indonesian equities for 31 August 2026. It notes that the Jakarta Composite Index (IHSG) closed at 6,518.12, down 0.12% on 28 August, with weekly lows of 6,376.65 and sector declines in technology (‑1.95%), transportation (‑1.89%) and property (‑1.62%). The recommended companies are: BRI Danareksa Sekuritas – BBNI, BFIN, VKTR; BNI Sekuritas – CUAN, BRPT, TPIA, ENRG, TAPG, FORE; Phintraco Sekuritas – BBCA, TLKM, DSSA, BBRI, EXCL; Phillip Sekuritas – TSPC, BMRI; MNC Sekuritas – AMRT, BUMI, INDF, LSIP; CGS International Sekuritas – INDY, MDKA, EMAS, BFIN, PWON, MAPA; Panin Sekuritas – MAPI, BBYB, SMRA; Mirae Asset Sekuritas – BBRI, CTRA, ENRG. Trading volume reached 150.03 billion shares with a transaction value of Rp 61.22 trillion across 8.68 million trades.

results.title: IHSG September 2026 Outlook Highlights Potential Weakness and Lists Recommended Stocks
results.body: The article forecasts that Indonesia’s Composite Index (IHSG) may face limited upside and heightened volatility in September 2026, with Kiwoom Sekuritas estimating a 40‑45% chance of a positive close within a 6,400‑6,705 range. Historical data shows the average September return over the past ten years weakened by 0.94%, and Kiwoom projects a 43% probability of the index testing 6,750 and an exit level near 6,230. Technical analysis from Mirae Asset Sekuritas Indonesia suggests the uptrend remains intact, citing positive MA20/60 crossovers, Stochastics K/D signals and a potential RSI golden cross, while also recommending a list of stocks including BBCA, BBNI, BBRI, BMRI, BBTN, CPIN, CTRA, INDF, ITMG, JSMR, TPIA, EXCL. Kiwoom Sekuritas adds target prices for INCO (6,300), ANTM (4,800), PANi (9,925), BBRI (3,600), MTEL (705), JSMR (3,850), JPFA (3,140), KLBF (970) and BBNI (4,100). The outlook notes global risks such as ECB and Fed policy decisions, US Treasury yields around 4.6‑4.7% for ten‑year bonds, and a 34% FedWatch probability of a September rate hike, which could pressure growth‑oriented and technology stocks.

results.title: Capex race among TLKM, EXCL and ISAT: assessing which telecom is best positioned for return
results.body: The article compares the large‑scale capital‑expenditure programmes of Indonesia’s three listed telecom operators—PT Telkom Indonesia (Persero) Tbk. (TLKM), PT Smart Telecom Sejahtera Tbk. (EXCL) and PT Indosat Ooredoo Hutchison Tbk. (ISAT)—and evaluates which is most likely to generate a timely return. TLKM plans to spend up to 20 % of revenue on capex through 2026, targeting cellular, fiber and data‑center projects, with a cash‑capex coverage of about 2.6 times its operating cash flow (TTM Rp64.4 trillion) and EBITDA contribution from its NeutraDC data centre expected to become visible in 2027. EXCL raised its 2026 capex guidance to Rp20 trillion to fund the XL‑Link Net integration, reporting 26 % semester‑I 2026 revenue growth and a normalized EBITDA increase of 19 %, while ISAT lifted its 2026 capex from Rp13 trillion to Rp23 trillion for 5G rollout, posting Q2‑2026 revenue growth of 14 % and ARPU growth of 19.5 %. Analysts note that the high capex levels could pressure free‑cash‑flow, especially for ISAT where capex rose 77 %, and that the speed of return will depend on the type of infrastructure, with data‑center projects offering the quickest payback.

results.title: IHSG opens higher as market concerns ease
results.body: The Jakarta Composite Index (IHSG) opened stronger on 28 August 2026 as easing market concerns lifted sentiment. At 09:01 the index rose 13.96 points, or 0.21%, to 6,535, with trading volume of about 3 billion shares and a transaction value of Rp1.3 trillion. Brokers highlighted several stocks for the session, naming EXCL, INET, HRUM (BRI Danareksa), BMRI, BBNI, INDY, CUAN, MBMA (Phintraco), ISAT, AADI, ADMR, ARCI, BBRI, BBNI (CGS International), and PANI, EMTK, ERAA (Panin Sekuritas) as preferred picks. Analysts projected the index to trade within support levels of 6,360‑6,400 and resistance of 6,600‑6,630, noting a technical rebound from the 20‑day moving average at 6,359 and positive MACD momentum.

results.title: Daily stock recommendation roundup for 28 August 2026
results.body: The article provides a summary of stock recommendations for 28 August 2026. results.title: BRI Danareksa Sekuritas recommends EXCL, INET and HRUM with bullish technical targets on 28 Aug 2026
results.body: BRI Danareksa Sekuritas issued a broker recommendation on 28 August 2026 for three Indonesian equities – EXCL, INET and HRUM – citing bullish technical setups. EXCL broke out above the 2,600 level and its MA20, pulled back to 2,639‑2,707 and now targets 2,840‑2,910, while announcing the resignation of commissioner Vivek Sood. INET reversed lower, broke its neckline at 240 and surged to a breakout at 338 on high volume, setting a target range of 358‑370 and noting foreign investor buying of Rp 23.9 billion in the regular market. HRUM rebounded above its MA20 after a breakout at 895, with near‑term targets of 935 and 975, support at 895‑863, and announced an extraordinary shareholders’ meeting on 18 September 2026 at the Deutsche Bank Building in Jakarta.

results.title: Foreign investors net bought ten Indonesian stocks as the IDX Composite fell 1.48%
results.body: The article reports that despite the IDX Composite (IHSG) dropping 1.48% to 6,405.69 points on 26 August 2026, foreign investors recorded a net purchase of about Rp 1.37 trillion in Indonesian equities. The ten stocks with the largest foreign net buys were PT Bank Central Asia Tbk, BMRI, EXCL, MDKA, DSSA, ICBP, PSAB, BRMS, ADRO and ASII. Foreign net buying amounts ranged from Rp 1.41 trillion for DSSA down to Rp 15.8 billion for ASII, with PT Bank Central Asia Tbk receiving Rp 80.82 billion. The market saw 583 stocks decline, total volume of 41.53 billion shares and transaction value of Rp 17.97 trillion, while sector indices fell between 0.73% and 4.15%.

results.title: Foreign investors net bought Rp 1.37 trillion on Wednesday, PT Dian Swastatika Sentosa Tbk topping the list as the IHSG dropped 1.48%
results.body: Foreign investors recorded a net purchase of Rp 1.37 trillion in Indonesian equities on 26 August 2026 despite the IHSG falling sharply. The IHSG closed down 1.48% (95.86 points) at 6,405.68, with 583 stocks declining, 118 rising, and total turnover of 41.53 billion shares worth Rp 17.97 trillion. The ten stocks with the largest foreign net buys were PT Dian Swastatika Sentosa Tbk (Rp 1.41 trillion), PT Bank Mandiri Tbk (Rp 257.32 billion), PT XL SMART Telecom Sejahtera Tbk (Rp 246.55 billion), PT Merdeka Copper Gold Tbk (Rp 119.15 billion), PT Bank Central Asia Tbk (Rp 80.82 billion), PT Indofood CBP Sukses Makmur Tbk (Rp 30.2 billion), PT J Resources Asia Pasifik Tbk (Rp 24.74 billion), PT Bumi Resources Minerals Tbk (Rp 23.55 billion), PT Alamtri Resources Indonesia Tbk (Rp 17.9 billion) and PT Astra International Tbk (Rp 15.8 billion). The foreign net buying underscores strong demand for these issuers even as overall market sentiment remained bearish.

results.title: PT Dayamitra Telekomunikasi Tbk (MTEL) gains new growth catalyst from spectrum allocation and sees merger talks with TBIG resurface
results.body: PT Dayamitra Telekomunikasi Tbk (MTEL) receives a fresh growth catalyst as additional spectrum allocations to telecom operators raise expectations for higher target prices and revive merger discussions with PT Tower Bersama Infrastructure Tbk (TBIG). The allocations of 255 MHz to PT Telkom Indonesia Tbk (TLKM), 205 MHz to PT Indosat Tbk (ISAT) and 217 MHz to PT XL Smart Telecom Sejahtera Tbk (EXCL) are expected to increase demand for colocation, new tower construction, fiber‑to‑the‑tower expansion and power‑as‑a‑service offerings for MTEL. MTEL now operates 40,563 towers (up 2 % YoY) serving 63,866 tenants (up 4.9 % YoY) with a tenancy ratio of 1.57, and its fiber network has grown to 59,239 km (up 8.8 % YoY) generating Rp309 billion in revenue (up 7.7 % YoY), representing roughly 54 % of the national fiber market. Analyst Christian Sitorus of MNC Sekuritas cites these operational trends as justification for a higher valuation of MTEL. The resurfaced merger plan with TBIG could further consolidate the tower and fiber businesses, potentially enhancing MTEL’s market position.

results.title: Indo Premier Sekuritas (IPOT) issues weekly stock recommendations for August 24‑28, 2026
results.body: Indo Premier Sekuritas (IPOT) released its weekly stock picks for the trading week of 24‑28 August 2026, anticipating a bullish technical momentum for the IHSG. The firm expects the index to stay above MA5‑MA100, with support at 6,429‑6,475 and a target range of 6,628‑6,666, while credit growth of 13.0% YoY in July supports domestic sentiment. IPOT recommends buying EXCL (entry Rp 2,840, target Rp 3,150, stop‑loss Rp 2,690), DSNG (entry Rp 1,440, target Rp 1,610, stop‑loss Rp 1,380), and BBNI on pull‑back (entry Rp 3,640‑3,700, target Rp 4,000, stop‑loss Rp 3,500) based on technical signals such as Doji candles, ADX above 20, EMA crossovers and a golden‑cross MACD. The broker also suggests the Premier ETF Gold Sharia Indonesia (XGLD) as a Sharia‑compliant gold exposure.

results.title: Rupiah and Indonesia's IHSG rise after President Prabowo's speech
results.body: The Indonesian rupiah and the Jakarta Composite Index (IHSG) strengthened after President Prabowo Subianto delivered his state address. IHSG opened at 6,296.59 points, then closed at 6,337.19, up 35.42 points (0.56%), while the rupiah traded around Rp17,839 per US dollar, up 38 points (0.21%). Nine of eleven sectors traded in the green, led by raw materials (+1.67%), infrastructure (+1.45%) and consumer staples (+1.17%). PT Vale Indonesia Tbk rose 6.50% to Rp5,325, PT XL SMART Telecom Sejahtera Tbk gained 5.70% to Rp2,780, and PT Alamtri Minerals Tbk increased 4.46% to Rp1,640. Market analysts said the president’s remarks, especially the mention of state‑owned enterprises, boosted investor sentiment.

results.title: IHSG closes weaker 1.13% at 6,301.77, pressured by MSCI rebalancing announcement
results.body: The Jakarta Composite Index (IHSG) closed Thursday down 1.13% at 6,301.77 as MSCI Inc.’s rebalancing announcement will remove PT Charoen Pokphand Indonesia Tbk. (CPIN) and PT GoTo Gojek Tokopedia Tbk. (GOTO) from the MSCI Global Standard Indexes. Of the 474 constituents that fell, PT Merdeka Battery Materials Tbk. (MBMA) dropped 7.27% to Rp510, PT ESSA Industries Indonesia Tbk. (ESSA) 7.04% to Rp660, and PT Vale Indonesia Tbk. (INCO) 5.21% to Rp5,000, while PT XLSMART Telecom Sejahtera Tbk. (EXCL) rose 2.73% to Rp2,630, PT Bank Negara Indonesia (Persero) Tbk. (BBNI) 0.84% to Rp3,610, and PT Bank Tabungan Negara (Persero) Tbk. (BBTN) 0.83% to Rp1,220. CPIN fell 1.59% to Rp3,100 after its downgrade to the MSCI Global Small Cap Index, and nine other Indonesian stocks were also removed from that index. Net foreign selling in the market reached Rp70.42 trillion through 12 August 2026, highlighting the liquidity concerns raised by market observers.

results.title: PT XL Smart Telecom Sejahtera Tbk reports USD153 million merger synergies, reduced net loss and increased 5G capex in 1H 2026
results.body: PT XL Smart Telecom Sejahtera Tbk disclosed that post‑merger synergies amounted to USD 153 million in the first half of 2026, helping narrow its consolidated net loss. Revenue grew 26% year‑on‑year to Rp24.03 trillion, while normalized EBITDA rose 19% to Rp11.05 trillion (46% margin) and normalized PAT jumped 294% to Rp2.73 trillion. Despite the improvement, the company still posted a net loss of Rp994 billion, better than the Rp1.2 trillion loss in the same period a year earlier, as integration costs, accelerated depreciation and asset impairments persisted. EXCL increased its 2026 capital‑expenditure target to Rp20 trillion (up from Rp15 trillion) to fund 5G expansion, with 1H capex of Rp10.27 trillion and gross debt of Rp20.87 trillion, resulting in a net‑debt‑to‑EBITDA ratio of 2.61×, while 90% of its loans remain floating‑rate.

results.title: Indonesia's IHSG drops 1.18% to 6,298 in Session I, with ESSA, MBMA, and CUAN leading LQ45 losses
results.body: The Jakarta Stock Exchange's composite index (IHSG) fell 1.18% (75.50 points) to 6,298.34 in the first trading session on Thursday, August 13, 2026, after MSCI announced a review and rebalancing. All sectoral indices weakened, led by raw materials down 2.48% and health care down 2.18%, adding pressure to the broader market. Among LQ45 constituents, PT ESSA Industries Indonesia Tbk slipped 7.75% to Rp 655, PT Merdeka Battery Mineral Tbk fell 5.45% to Rp 520, and PT Petrindo Jaya Kreasi Tbk dropped 4.60% to Rp 830, making them the top losers. Meanwhile, PT Indika Energy Tbk rose 2.42% to Rp 2,540, PT Indosat Tbk gained 1.63% to Rp 2,500, and PT XL SMART Telecom Sejahtera Tbk increased 1.56% to Rp 2,600, leading the LQ45 gainers.

results.title: EXCL reports normalized profit surges and net loss narrows in H1 2026
results.body: The article reports that PT XLSmart Telecom Sejahtera Tbk (EXCL) posted a four‑fold increase in normalized net profit while its consolidated net loss narrowed in the first half of 2026. Normalized net profit rose to Rp2.7 trillion from Rp693 billion a year earlier, whereas the consolidated net loss was Rp994 billion, down from Rp1.2 trillion in H1 2025. Quarterly results showed a Q2 2026 net loss of Rp277 billion, an improvement from Rp1.6 trillion in Q2 2025, and normalized profit of Rp1.3 trillion, with EBITDA reaching Rp5.5 trillion (+24% YoY) and cumulative EBITDA for H1 2026 at Rp11 trillion (45.7% margin). Revenue grew 26% YoY to Rp24 trillion, meeting 52% of the 2026 consensus, and management raised its 2026 capex guidance to Rp20 trillion to fund a new spectrum acquisition.

results.title: Today's Stock Recommendations: PTRO, BRPT, and TUGU
results.body: The article presents Mega Capital Sekuritas' stock recommendations for PTRO, BRPT and TUGU amid a strong market session where the IHSG rose 1.69% to 6,373.85 on 12 August 2026. It notes that BRPT gained 7.14% while foreign investors recorded net purchases of Rp482.79 billion in the regular market and highlights MSCI’s August 2026 Index Review, which removes GOTO from the Global Standard Index, shifts CPIN to the Small‑Cap Index and drops BANK, BUKA, ESSA, FILM, HEAL, KPIG, RATU, SMGR and TCPI from the MSCI Indonesia Small‑Cap Index effective 31 August 2026. The report also details XLSMART Telecom Sejahtera (EXCL) posting a 25.6% YoY revenue increase to Rp23.99 trillion, a 41.1% rise in EBITDA to Rp11.34 trillion and a narrowed net loss of Rp998.06 billion for the first half of 2026. Indonesian Paradise Property (INPP) announced an interim cash dividend of Rp4.5 per share (89.23% payout ratio) with a dividend yield of about 0.60% based on its closing price of Rp750, and its first‑half net profit rose to Rp56.39 billion.
